newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex narrows first half loss, unclear on future.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex narrows first half loss, unclear on future.

text.p: French appliance maker Moulinex cut losses in the first half of its 1996/97 year by 38 percent but said Friday the benefits of a restructuring programme would not be seen for a year.
It said its loss narrowed to 74 million French francs ($14 million) in the six months to Sept. 30 from 121 million ($24 million).

In the 1995/96 year to March 31, Moulinex reported a loss of 702 million francs ($135 million), its fourth consecutive annual loss, after taking a 600 million franc ($115 million) charge for the restructuring plan.
Chairman Pierre Blayau said he did not expect to see before 1997/98 tangible results of a restructuring plan unveiled in June.
The company has planned to cut 2,600 jobs, or more than 20 percent of the staff, and close two plants. About 2,100 jobs will be cut in France and the rest in Germany, where layoffs have begun.
